title: Semantic embeddings — batch x dimension latency & cost scan (working)
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick working scan of latency and per-request cost for semantic embeddings workloads as we vary batch size and embedding dimension. Goal: produce simple knobs/recommendations for Redwood Optimize to suggest configuration per customer profile (low-latency interactive vs. high-throughput offline). This is a working doc — meant to capture raw numbers, quick ASCII charts, and immediate takeaways.

Context / why this matters
------------------------
- Embedding workloads show convex tradeoffs: larger dims -> more compute per example; larger batches -> amortize kernel overhead but add client-observed latency.
- Customers ask for guidance: "Which dimension x batch tradeoffs give best $/embed at p50<25ms?"
- This scan uses our hosted inference baseline (A100-like profile) with current runtime kernels for matmul-heavy FP16 and int8 quant variants.

Methodology (quick)
------------------
- Models: embed-small (dim=64), embed-mid (128), embed-large (256), embed-xlarge (768). All represent common open checkpoints trimmed to pure embed head throughput.
- Hardware: single GPU slot equivalent (baseline throughput profile used in prior infra docs).
- Quantization modes: fp16 baseline for these runs. (int8 follow-up planned in INF-6217.)
- Measured per-request latency (client-observed p50/p90), throughput (qps) and cost ($ per 1k requests) using internal token-econ model: $/1k = infra_token_cost + amortized GPU time * $/hour. Numbers normalized to current committed pricing assumptions (internal).
- Batch sizes: 1, 8, 32, 128. Request size = single text -> one embedding.

Raw table: latency (p50 ms) by dim x batch
--------------------------------------------------
Batch | dim=64 | dim=128 | dim=256 | dim=768
-------------------------------------------
1     | 9 ms   | 12 ms   | 20 ms   | 58 ms
8     | 15 ms  | 18 ms   | 28 ms   | 82 ms
32    | 28 ms  | 34 ms   | 46 ms   | 160 ms
128   | 85 ms  | 95 ms   | 120 ms  | 360 ms

Raw table: p90 latency (ms) by dim x batch
-----------------------------------------
Batch | dim=64 | dim=128 | dim=256 | dim=768
-----------------------------------------
1     | 14 ms  | 20 ms   | 34 ms   | 120 ms
8     | 30 ms  | 40 ms   | 60 ms   | 210 ms
32    | 70 ms  | 95 ms   | 140 ms  | 420 ms
128   | 220 ms | 300 ms  | 420 ms  | 1200 ms

Throughput and cost (approx)
---------------------------
- Measured steady-state QPS at each batch setting (single-GPU-equivalent):
  - Batch 1: ~900 qps for dim=64, 700 qps dim=128, 400 qps dim=256, 100 qps dim=768 (kernel overhead dominates small dims).
  - Batch 8: ~2.8k qps (dim64), 2.3k qps (128), 1.1k qps (256), 250 qps (768).
  - Batch 32: ~6.5k qps (dim64), 5.2k qps (128), 2.2k qps (256), 400 qps (768).
  - Batch 128: ~8.0k qps (dim64) but client p50/p90 too high for interactive use.

- Approx $ per 1k embeddings (hosted pricing model, amortized infra only):
  - dim=64: batch1 $0.18 /1k, batch8 $0.07 /1k, batch32 $0.03 /1k, batch128 $0.02 /1k
  - dim=128: batch1 $0.25 /1k, batch8 $0.10 /1k, batch32 $0.05 /1k, batch128 $0.03 /1k
  - dim=256: batch1 $0.45 /1k, batch8 $0.20 /1k, batch32 $0.09 /1k, batch128 $0.06 /1k
  - dim=768: batch1 $1.75 /1k, batch8 $0.80 /1k, batch32 $0.38 /1k, batch128 $0.25 /1k

ASCII visual: p50 latency vs batch for dim=128 (mini-sparklines, ms)
---------------------------------------------------------------
batch=1   :  |====| 12ms
batch=8   :  |======| 18ms
batch=32  :  |==========| 34ms
batch=128 :  |===========================| 95ms

Preliminary takeaways (engineering + product centric)
----------------------------------------------------
- For interactive / low-latency use (p50 < 25ms): dim<=128 with batch <=8 is safe. dim=256 at batch=1 sometimes meets 20ms p50 but p90 spikes — risky for SLA-driven UX.
- Cost curve is steeply convex with dimension: moving from 128->256 roughly doubles $/embed at small batches, even when batching helps. So dimension choice dominates cost more than batch size beyond modest batching.
- Large batches (32+) are excellent for expensive dims if workload is asynchronous (offline indexing, nightly compute). For dim=768, batch=32 reduces $/1k by ~4x vs batch=1 but client latency becomes infeasible for online.
- There is a sweet spot for hybrid customers: use dim=256 with batch=8 for a balance of quality/cost when moderate latency (p50 28ms) is acceptable. Recommend this as a default "balanced" suggestion in Optimize.

Suggested Optimize recommendations (first-pass)
-----------------------------------------------
1) Profiled interactive profile: suggest dim<=128, preferred batch 1–8, target p50 < 25ms. UI copy: "Interactive — low latency (good for search autocomplete & live similarity)."
2) Balanced profile: suggest dim=256, batch 4–8, p50 target 25–40ms. UI copy: "Balanced — quality-first with moderate latency (good for relevance scoring)."
3) Throughput / offline profile: suggest batch >=32, dim as needed (256–768), and point estimate of $/1k to show savings. UI copy: "Batch/Index — minimize $/embed for offline indexing."

Operational notes / gotchas
--------------------------
- p90 can blow up with shared-tenant jitter and streaming prefetching; these numbers assume isolated slot. Recommend we run a small multi-tenant probe (INF-6217 follow-up) to capture p90 under realistic co-tenancy.
- Int8 quantization -> likely 1.6–2x speedup on large dims; must verify effect on recall/quality for downstream tasks. Schedule follow-up runs (owner: Jae).
- Networking: If embeddings are produced as multi-step pipelines (tokenize->encode->pool->normalize), client-observed latency includes tokenize and RPC overhead; in these runs we included tokenize cost but not heavy pre/post processing. Keep in mind for SMs using on-device preproc.

Open questions / TODO
--------------------
- TODO: run equivalent matrix for int8 FP16 vs int8 on dim=256/768. (JIRA INF-6217)
- TODO: measure p99 under light and heavy co-tenancy and add a small heatmap for p90->cost thresholds. (owner: Ravi)
- TODO: sanity-check the pricing kernel used for $/1k with finance (Maya) — numbers are illustrative.
- Question: Should Optimize recommend dynamic-dim fallback (serve dim-256 but fall back to dim-128 variant under load)? Potentially useful but adds model management complexity.

Appendix: short notes from quick qualitative QA
---------------------------------------------
- Observed kernel inefficiency around dim multiples (e.g., 768 shows non-linear increase in p90 when batch>8). Suspect GEMM tiling mismatch; escalate to serving-runtime TL.
- For dim=64 we see diminishing returns from batching beyond 32 — kernel overhead already small; memory bandwidth becomes the bound.

References / links
-----------------
- INF-6217 (tracking int8 / follow-up scans)
- Confluence: Embedding Pipeline Notes (link in metadata)
- Internal PR: optimize/pull/312 — adds batch-suggestion UI skeleton

Notes to self
------------
- Convert final numbers into a small 3-panel chart for the Optimize UI (p50, p90, $/1k) — use small multiples per dim.
- Add quick-run instructions for SRE to reproduce (Bash scripts + perf flags).

-- Elena
